issues.legal_issue: A reference court lacks jurisdiction to reopen a completed compensation decree to award additional statutory benefits through a fresh application rather than a permitted correction.
material_facts: A court hearing a land acquisition compensation reference had made an award enhancing compensation, and that award had become final.
After an amendment introduced additional compensation benefits, the claimants applied to the reference court for those benefits.
The application sought substantive additional relief, not correction of a clerical or arithmetic mistake.
The reference court allowed the application, and the High Court summarily dismissed the State’s appeal.
issues.conclusion: The reference court lacked jurisdiction to entertain the application for additional benefits; its order was void. The Supreme Court set aside the orders of the reference court and the High Court and dismissed the application.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 18 and 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the reference court determines compensation within the powers conferred by the Act. Under section 26(2), its award is deemed a decree. After that decree, correction is confined to the statutory correction power under section 13-A of the Act and section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Section 151 CPC, which preserves inherent power to prevent abuse of process or meet the ends of justice, does not confer jurisdiction to grant fresh substantive relief where the Act expressly defines the court’s powers. The additional amounts under section 23(1-A) and (2) are additional to, rather than components of, the compensation determined under section 23(1); interest under section 28 is consequential on an enhancement of compensation. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_reference and final_compensation_decree and post_decree_application and seeks_new_substantive_benefits and not limited_to_permitted_correction

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_reference: The proceeding is a court reference to determine compensation for acquired land.
predicates.final_compensation_decree: The court has made a compensation award that has become a decree.
predicates.post_decree_application: A party applies for relief after the compensation decree has been made.
predicates.seeks_new_substantive_benefits: The application seeks additional compensation benefits rather than enforcement of relief already awarded.
predicates.limited_to_permitted_correction: The application is confined to correcting a clerical or arithmetic error in the decree.
predicates.reference_court_lacks_jurisdiction_to_aw: The reference court has no jurisdiction to award new substantive benefits after the compensation decree.

issues.definition: When a party in a land acquisition compensation reference applies after a final compensation decree for new substantive benefits rather than a permitted correction, the reference court lacks jurisdiction to award those benefits.
